findings.title: The /workbench-layouts/ route bypasses the symlink guard: serveWorkbenchLayouts checks containment textually and the guard does not map that URL prefix, so a symlink under _data/workbench/layouts/ pointing outside is served.
findings.evidence: ts/vite.config.ts:134-150 (serveWorkbenchLayouts, no realpath) and :71-78 (candidates() maps only /@fs/ and root-relative under ts/). Reproduced with an untracked symlink: GET /workbench-layouts/evil-layout.json -> 200 with the outside file; the same file via /@fs -> 403.
findings.consequence: The goal of the owner ruling (no symlink under the allow-listed directories is served) is not met for a live route.

findings.title: The guard checks a path and then hands the request on, so the check and the read are not atomic; swapping a file and a symlink under concurrent requests crashed the dev server with an unhandled stream error.
findings.evidence: Toggle of ts/public/race.txt between a regular file and a symlink under about 600 concurrent requests: Node v22.22.2 unhandled ReadStream error ENOENT; the server process exited. The builder later measured secret responses on guarded paths in the same race.
findings.consequence: Denial of service and, per the builder's follow-up probe, disclosure under a race, for anyone who can write under ts/ or _data/workbench/.
